title: Getting to Lumbini: Flights, Roads and the Border
meta_description: How to get to Lumbini: flights to Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa, roads from Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan, and crossing from India.
summary: The quickest way to Lumbini is a 35-minute flight from Kathmandu to Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa, then 22 km by road. By road it is about 280 km and 8–10 hours from Kathmandu, 7–8 hours from Pokhara and 4–5 hours from Chitwan. From India, cross at Belahiya–Sunauli, about 30 km away.

sections.heading: Where Lumbini is
paras: Lumbini is in Rupandehi district in Lumbini Province, on the flat Terai plains of south-western Nepal, at about 110 m. The nearest city is Siddharthanagar, still universally called Bhairahawa, about 22 km to the east. Bhairahawa is the gateway: it has the airport, the bus park, banks and the road south to the Indian border at Belahiya–Sunauli.

Lumbini itself has two parts that matter to visitors. The Lumbini development zone holds the Sacred Garden, the monastic zones and the museum. Next to it, the small town of Lumbini Bazaar, also called Buddhanagar, has guesthouses, restaurants, shops and the local bus stop. Most hotels are in or around these two areas.

sections.heading: By air: Gautam Buddha International Airport
paras: Gautam Buddha International Airport, code BWA, sits on the edge of Bhairahawa. It was upgraded from a domestic airport and opened for international flights in May 2022, on Buddha Jayanti, with a runway long enough for large jets. It is Nepal's second international airport after Kathmandu.

Domestic flights from Kathmandu take about 35 minutes and run several times a day with Nepali airlines such as Buddha Air and Yeti Airlines. On a clear day, sit on the right side flying south-west from Kathmandu for a view back to the Himalaya. Foreign passengers pay a US dollar fare that is higher than the Nepali one; book ahead in the winter pilgrim season and around festivals.

International services have been limited since the airport opened. Several airlines have started and later suspended routes, so most international visitors still arrive in Kathmandu and connect on a domestic flight. Routes change often, so check current status before you travel.

From the airport, Lumbini is about 22 km west, 30–40 minutes by car. Taxis wait outside arrivals; agree the fare before you get in, or book a transfer through your hotel. If you are travelling with us, your guide and driver meet you at arrivals.

sections.heading: By road from Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan
paras: From Kathmandu the road is about 280 km. It follows the Prithvi Highway west down the Trishuli valley to Mugling, turns south to Narayangarh, runs west along the East-West Highway to Butwal, then south to Bhairahawa and west to Lumbini. Allow 8–10 hours by private car and longer by bus, especially if road works on the Mugling–Narayangarh stretch cause delays. Tourist buses and ordinary buses both run this route daily.

From Pokhara, take the Siddhartha Highway south through Syangja, across the Kali Gandaki and over the hills to Tansen and Butwal, about 180 km and 7–8 hours. The road is winding and scenic; breaking the journey with a night in Tansen makes it far more comfortable.

From Chitwan, the road from Sauraha runs to Narayangarh and then west along the East-West Highway through Nawalparasi to Butwal and Bhairahawa, about 160 km and 4–5 hours. On the way you pass close to Ramagrama and Devdaha, which can be visited as stops with a little extra time.

sections.heading: Distances and times at a glance
paras: Times are for a private car in normal conditions. Add time for buses, fog in winter and landslides or road works in the monsoon.

sections.heading: From India via Sunauli
paras: Many pilgrims reach Lumbini from India as part of the Buddhist circuit. The main crossing is Sunauli on the Indian side and Belahiya on the Nepal side, about 4 km south of Bhairahawa and about 30 km from Lumbini. Gorakhpur, the nearest large Indian city and railway junction, is about 95 km south of the border. Kushinagar, where the Buddha died, is about 150 km away and has its own airport.

Indian citizens do not need a visa for Nepal but should carry valid photo identification. Other foreign nationals must get an Indian exit stamp at Sunauli and a Nepal visa and entry stamp at Belahiya, where visas on arrival are available to most nationalities. Coming the other way, you need an Indian visa in advance, and the rules on which Indian visas are valid at land borders change, so check current status before you travel.

The border is crowded with trucks, rickshaws and touts from mid-morning. Cross early, keep documents together and agree prices before taking any ride. Shared jeeps and buses run from Bhairahawa to Lumbini through the day.

sections.heading: Getting around once you arrive
paras: The Lumbini development zone is about 4.8 km long, and the sites are spread out. Within it, cars are restricted and the Sacred Garden itself is closed to traffic, so most visitors move by bicycle, e-rickshaw or cycle rickshaw. Bicycles can be hired near the main gate and through hotels; e-rickshaws wait at the gates and can be hired by the hour or for a set route.

For trips outside Lumbini, to Tilaurakot, Ramagrama, Devdaha or Tansen, a private car with a driver is the practical choice. Local buses do reach Taulihawa and Parasi, but connections to the actual sites are slow and irregular, and the heat makes waiting by the roadside hard work from March onwards.
list: Carry Nepali rupees in cash; cards work in larger hotels but rarely elsewhere
ATMs are reliable in Bhairahawa and available in Lumbini Bazaar
Save your hotel's phone number for drivers, as addresses are informal
In December and January, allow extra time for morning fog on roads and at the airport

sections.heading: Where to stay when you arrive
paras: Stay in Lumbini rather than Bhairahawa if you can. Being close to the Sacred Garden lets you walk in at dawn and at dusk, the two best times, without a drive. Buddha Maya Garden Hotel is close to the zone and has gardens and quiet rooms; Lumbini Hokke Hotel, inside the development area, was built with Japanese pilgrims in mind and is calm and simple. Lumbini Bazaar has many budget guesthouses. Book early for December to February and for Buddha Jayanti, when pilgrim groups fill the better hotels.

Bhairahawa makes sense only for a very early flight or a late arrival from the border. It has larger business hotels and more restaurants, but it is a busy trading town and the drive to the Sacred Garden takes 30–40 minutes each way.

sections.heading: Which way should you come?
paras: If time is short, fly. The flight saves a full day each way, and the airport is close to Lumbini. If you have time and want to see the country, drive at least one way: down from Pokhara through Tansen, or across the plains from Chitwan. Each road shows a different Nepal, from Magar hill villages to Tharu farms. If you are continuing to India's Buddhist sites, plan to leave via Sunauli, and let the border be the next step rather than a detour.

Whatever you choose, give Lumbini at least one full night. Day trips from Kathmandu by air are possible, and some travellers do them, but they leave you in the Sacred Garden at midday, in the heat and the crowds, and miss the quiet hours that make the place what it is.

faqs.q: What is the nearest airport to Lumbini?
faqs.a: Gautam Buddha International Airport, code BWA, at Bhairahawa (Siddharthanagar), about 22 km east of Lumbini, roughly 30–40 minutes by car. It handles domestic flights from Kathmandu and has had some international services since it opened as an international airport in May 2022. International routes change often, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long is the flight from Kathmandu to Lumbini?
faqs.a: The flight from Kathmandu to Bhairahawa takes about 35 minutes, with several departures a day on Nepali airlines such as Buddha Air and Yeti Airlines. Add 30–40 minutes by road from the airport to Lumbini. Morning flights can be delayed by fog in December and January, so leave buffer time for onward connections.

faqs.q: How long does it take to drive from Kathmandu to Lumbini?
faqs.a: About 8–10 hours by private car for roughly 280 km, via Mugling, Narayangarh and Butwal. Buses take longer. Road works and traffic on the Mugling–Narayangarh section can add hours, and winter fog slows the plains stretch. Many travellers break the trip with a night in Chitwan or fly instead.

faqs.q: Can I take a bus from Kathmandu to Lumbini?
faqs.a: Yes. Tourist buses and ordinary buses run from Kathmandu to Bhairahawa and some continue to Lumbini, usually leaving early in the morning and taking 9–11 hours. Night buses also run but are less comfortable and less safe. From Bhairahawa, local buses and shared jeeps run to Lumbini Bazaar through the day.

faqs.q: How do I get from Pokhara to Lumbini?
faqs.a: By road along the Siddhartha Highway through Tansen and Butwal, about 180 km and 7–8 hours by private car, longer by bus. There are no regular direct flights between Pokhara and Bhairahawa. We recommend breaking the journey with a night in Tansen, an old hill town with good views and craft workshops.

faqs.q: How far is Lumbini from the Indian border?
faqs.a: The Belahiya–Sunauli border crossing is about 30 km from Lumbini, 45 minutes to an hour by car via Bhairahawa. Gorakhpur in India is about 95 km beyond the border, and Kushinagar about 150 km. Non-Indian foreigners need the correct visas and immigration stamps on both sides; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa to enter Nepal at Belahiya?
faqs.a: Most foreign nationals can get a Nepal visa on arrival at Belahiya, paying the fee for 15, 30 or 90 days. Indian citizens do not need a visa but should carry a passport or voter ID. Visa fees and rules change, so check current status before you travel, and carry passport photos and cash for the fee.

faqs.q: How do I get around Lumbini?
faqs.a: By bicycle, e-rickshaw or cycle rickshaw. The development zone is about 4.8 km long and the Sacred Garden is closed to cars, so private vehicles are of limited use within it. Bicycles can be hired near the main gate and through hotels. For day trips to Tilaurakot, Ramagrama or Devdaha, hire a car with a driver.

faqs.q: Is there an ATM in Lumbini?
faqs.a: There are ATMs in Lumbini Bazaar and many more in Bhairahawa, which is the better place to withdraw larger amounts. Larger hotels accept cards, but small restaurants, rickshaws, entry counters and shops usually need cash in Nepali rupees. Withdraw enough in Bhairahawa or Kathmandu before heading out to the Kapilavastu sites.
